#14 [OPEN] POST /api/analyze returns 500 when the text contains a NUL byte
assignees: []
Found in judge-style rehearsal (deployed e0f72a2).

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud/api/analyze \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"five words here and \^@ then more words after it"}'
# 500
```

Cause: `psycopg.DataError: PostgreSQL text fields cannot contain NUL (0x00) bytes` from the text lookup (`api/store.py` `clusters_for_text`). Expected: strip NULs (or 422), never 500. The same probably applies to `handle` and `url`.
COMMENTS: []
-----
#15 [OPEN] /api/analyze ignores bsky.app post links: a post that is in a cluster comes back 'insufficient'
assignees: []
Judges will most likely paste a Bluesky post link. Today a link to a post that is in a stored cluster isn't matched:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud/api/analyze -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"url":"https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:qqkeo4lcj4vvsv26moyitw44/post/3n27wevn47t2i"}'
# status: insufficient, clusters: [], notes: 'The live web check returned nothing usable'
```
That post is one of cluster 682's posts (`GET /api/clusters/682`). `clusters_for_url` only compares against `embed_urls`, and `checkable_url` skips bsky.app hosts.

Expected: parse `bsky.app/profile/<handle|did>/post/<rkey>` (and `at://` URIs) into the post URI, match `cluster_posts`, and fall back to the author's DID/handle lookup.
COMMENTS: []
-----
#16 [OPEN] Ad-hoc /api/analyze web findings use cluster wording ('shared by 1 of 1 accounts', 'The cluster's message text')
assignees: []
For a judge's own input there is no cluster, but the web findings read as if there were:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud/api/analyze -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"url":"https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-37982000","text":"Tämä on täysin tavallinen suomenkielinen viesti junalakosta Helsingissä tänään."}'
# 'Linked page shared by 1 of 1 accounts: ...'
# 'The cluster's message text matches 8 web results on 6 domains ...'
```
Cause: `api/routes/analyze.py` runs `SourceChecker.check` on one synthetic `ClusterPost(did='adhoc')`, and `sources/checker.py` writes cluster summaries. Expected: input wording (e.g. 'The linked page: ...', 'Your text matches ...'), no account counts. Matters because analyze answers must read as weaker, input-level evidence.
COMMENTS: []
-----
#17 [OPEN] CJK/Thai text (no spaces) is never a content key or a web-search phrase
assignees: []
Word counts use whitespace splitting, so unspaced scripts never reach the thresholds:

```python
from signals.textnorm import normalize_text, tokens
t = '今日は東京で大雨が降っていて電車が止まっています。みんな気をつけてください。'
len(tokens(normalize_text(t)))          # 2  (needs min_text_tokens=5)
from sources.links import claim_phrase
claim_phrase([t])                       # None
```
Effects: Japanese/Chinese/Thai copy-paste campaigns get no `duplicate_text` / `near_duplicate_text` key (`signals/keys.py`), and `POST /api/analyze` answers 'Text too short ... (needs 5+ words)' for a long Japanese sentence. Japanese is ~4% of posts in a 10-minute window. Either use a character-based length/shingles for these scripts or list it as a known limit.
COMMENTS: []
-----
#18 [OPEN] Organic-guard text contradicts itself: 'on average only 100% ... (a wider crowd is doing the same thing)'
assignees: []
`part_of_wider_crowd` is stored and shown even when it scores 0 and says the opposite of its text. Example: `GET https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud/api/clusters/682` → signal `part_of_wider_crowd` (polarity against, score 0.0): 'on average only 100% of the accounts sharing these items in the window are in this cluster (a wider crowd is doing the same thing)'.

Evidence text is what judges read. Expected: when exclusivity is high, either skip the guard row or word it as the absence of a crowd ('all accounts sharing these items in the window are in this cluster'). `signals/score.py` `organic_guards`.
COMMENTS: []
-----
#19 [OPEN] Single-publisher feed accounts flip between coordinated and insufficient; transparent_automation misses them
assignees: []
Cluster 682 (and 859, same accounts, 1h window): 5 JD Supra topic-feed accounts (`techlawjdsupra`, `m-and-a-jdsupra`, `frank-jdsupra`, ... all on bsky.social) post the same jdsupra.com article about 1 s apart. At about 21:35 UTC it was listed as `coordinated` (🚩), and after enrichment at 21:38 it was `insufficient` (`established_accounts` = 0.6, two families fired), so the same accounts changed verdict within minutes.

This is one declared publisher's automation, not covert amplification. `transparent_automation` only fires on a shared custom handle domain (`sub.domain.tld`), so it doesn't see a brand token repeated in bsky.social handles or the shared publisher domain of the link. Suggested: treat 'all members post links to one domain and share a handle token' as transparent automation, and add the case to the organic tests. `signals/score.py`.
COMMENTS: []
-----
#20 [OPEN] Default Gemini model gemini-2.5-pro returns 404 (config default and .env.example)
assignees: []
`common/config.py` (`gemini_model`) and `.env.example` default to `gemini-2.5-pro`. With the team key the API answers `404 NOT_FOUND: This model models/gemini-2.5-pro is no longer available to new users`, so every analyst call fails. Production works only because its `.env` now sets `GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-4-argon` (verdicts appear since 21:41 UTC); a fresh deploy or a local run from `.env.example` writes no verdicts. Expected: default to a model that exists (gemini-4-argon is what production uses).
COMMENTS: []

## Workflow with Entire

- One Trail per feature: from your feature branch run `entire trail create --title "<what and why>" --type feature`. Commits pushed to that branch, and the agent sessions behind them, attach to the Trail.
- Commit agent work with the agent running, so Entire links the commit to its session (`Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer). Don't amend or rebase away those trailers.
- Before merging, run `entire review general`. It reviews locally with Claude Code (no Entire credit; Codex-only users ask a teammate to run it) and posts the verdict to the Trail. Fix or dismiss each finding, then open the PR with `entire trail ci-pr`, undraft it with `entire trail ready`, and squash-merge it while keeping the checkpoint trailers in the squash commit:

  ```bash
  gh pr merge <n> --squash --body "$(git log --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint)' origin/main..HEAD | grep . | sort -u)"
  ```

  A squash without those trailers loses the link between the commit on `main` and its agent sessions.
- Don't run `entire trail rerun-review` or enable project Agents on entire.com: those run paid cloud agents. Ask the repo owner first.
- Never paste keys or `.env` contents into a prompt: transcripts are stored in checkpoints.
======
# eval/: how often is the detector right?

Every number the dashboard shows about our own accuracy comes from here, through `eval_runs`
(`GET /api/metrics` serves the latest row per `dataset` + `split`).

```bash
uv run python -m eval copy-slices                                # keep finished recorded hours
uv run python -m eval recall --split dev --base-rates signals/fixtures/attack_results_live_v15_20261113T2000Z.json           # print the table only
uv run python -m eval recall --split heldout --base-rates signals/fixtures/attack_results_live_v15_20261113T2000Z.json \
    --database-url URL                                            # ...and write an eval_runs row
uv run pytest tests/test_eval_recall.py                           # offline; no DB, no network
```

For `recall`, `--database-url` is opt-in: without it nothing is written anywhere. Other flags:
`--repeats N` (campaigns per level per window, default 5), `--levels L1 L2`, `--workers 4`,
`--json-out FILE`, `--hours YYYYMMDDHH ...` (ad-hoc hours instead of a split). `--base-rates FILE`
turns on the detector's identity base-rate test (v1.5) the way the live worker runs it: the live
worker measures base rates from its DB (`signals.baseline.load_rates`), which the offline eval
can't reach, so it reads them from a JSON file (`BaseRates.as_dict()`, or any file with a
`base_rates` key, like Kirill's live measurement above). The source is stored in
`details.base_rates`; without the flag that is `null` and the identity test is off. Ad-hoc or partial runs (`--hours`,
`--max-windows`, a subset of `--levels`, a `--window-s` other than 600) are refused with
`--database-url`, so they can't replace a split's published row.

Organic false positives (`organic.py`, below):

```bash
uv run python -m eval organic select   # pick live organic cases -> eval/fixtures/organic_live.json
uv run python -m eval organic run      # print the report; no eval_runs rows
uv run python -m eval organic run --write [--database-url URL]  # ...and write eval_runs rows
uv run pytest tests/test_eval_organic.py                          # offline; no DB, no network
```

For `organic`, `--write` writes the rows (to `--database-url`, default `DATABASE_URL`). Every
run may add fetched profiles to the profile cache (`--offline` fetches nothing).

## Datasets and splits

| `dataset` | What it measures | Columns filled |
|---|---|---|
| `synthetic_campaigns` | **recall**: share of injected synthetic campaigns the detector marks `coordinated` | `recall`, `n`, `details` (`precision`, `f1`, `fpr` stay NULL: no negatives here) |
| `calibration` | **reliability**: coordination score vs coordination ground truth, and decided-verdict confidence vs correctness | `precision`, `recall`, `f1`, `fpr`, `n`, `details`; each reliability metric has its own eligible `n` |
| `live_hand_labels` | **precision** of `coordinated` and **FPR** on live clusters, against two humans' blind labels (below) | `precision`, `fpr`, `n` (definite human labels in that split), `details` (kappa, CIs, per-item labels) |
| `organic_synth` | **FPR**: share of injected synthetic organic bursts (viral, news link, live event, fandom) the detector marks `coordinated` | `fpr`, `n`, `details` |
| `organic_live` | **FPR** on real organic bursts in recorded windows, picked by a fixed rule that never reads detector output | `fpr`, `n`, `details` |
| `bluesky_takedowns` | **External validation**: share of accounts Bluesky itself takes down or suspends within `horizon_h` hours after we flag them, per detector status, vs. random active accounts (`eval/takedowns.py`, below) | `n` (eligible `coordinated` accounts), `details` (all groups, Wilson CIs, cluster-level table) |

`split` is `dev` (we may look at it while changing the detector or the eval) or `heldout`
(reported only; never tune thresholds, hit rules or synth settings on it). **Split rule** (shared
by every eval here): a window belongs to the UTC hour it starts in; **odd hours are `heldout`,
even hours are `dev`** (`eval/slices.py`, `split_of_hour`). Whole hours, so one burst never
straddles both. `--split` uses every recorded hour of that parity found under `--slice`; the hours
and windows actually used are stored in `details`.

Recorded hours kept so far (2026-11-13, UTC): 19 (`heldout`; recording began 19:41, so only the
19:50 window is complete), 20 (`dev`), 21 (`heldout`). Disclosure: the 19:50 window was used for
a one-window smoke test before the split rule was fixed; nothing was tuned on it.

The recorder keeps raw hours for 24 h only, so these hours are copied (same layout) to
`/srv/junction-espoo/data/eval-slices/jetstream/` on the team server (shared, outside git).

## How the recall eval works (`recall.py`)

1. **Windows** (`slices.py`): the recording is cut into clock-aligned 10-minute windows (the live
   worker's main window). Each window is built in memory with the ingest normaliser and the same
   rules as `signals.window.load_window`: posts in the window; likes/reposts/follows whose subject
   got 2..`max_key_accounts` distinct accounts; per-second background counts of every event; events
   duplicated across Jetstream hosts kept once. No database is involved. Windows the recording
   doesn't fully cover (start, end, or a hole over 60 s) are skipped and listed in `details`.
2. **Inject**: for each window, level (L1, L2, L3) and repeat, one campaign from
   `signals.synth.campaign` (12 accounts, `did:plc:synth*`, seeded per window/level/repeat) is
   added to the real window with `signals.synth.inject`. One campaign per detector run, so
   campaigns never help each other. Nothing is posted anywhere and nothing touches a database.
3. **Detect**: `signals.detect.detect`, the live worker's entry point and config. Only synthetic
   accounts get account info (age, followers...); real accounts in an offline window have none.
4. **Score**: a campaign is **caught** when >= 50% of its accounts are in clusters with status
   `coordinated`. **Surfaced** (reported, not counted as caught) = >= 50% in clusters the worker
   would store at any status, i.e. visible on the dashboard as "can't tell" or "chill". Recall =
   caught / injected, with a 95% Wilson interval, overall and per level.

Levels (from `signals/synth.py`): **L1** copy-paste text + link, brand-new templated accounts,
< 1 min burst. **L2** light paraphrase, 3-8 week old accounts, ~5 min jitter. **L3** heavy
paraphrase, aged accounts with followers, slow drip over the whole window.

`details` holds: `per_level` (caught, surfaced, CI, best-cluster status counts),
`detector_version`, `eval_commit`, `hit_rule`, the windows used and skipped, the baseline
cluster counts of each window without injection, and every trial.

```bash

set -a; . ~/.config/noise-radar/prod-db.env; set +a  # PROD_DATABASE_URL, via a private socket
```

**How to label.** Open the page (through an SSH tunnel: `ssh -L 8001:127.0.0.1:8001 <team server>`,
then http://127.0.0.1:8001/), type your name once, and judge each item on its own: a group of
accounts and everything they did in one time window (timeline, posts several of them engaged
with, repeated texts, links, follows, account ages, followers, avatars, their posts, with
bsky.app links). Press **1** coordinated (acting together; hard to explain as independent
people), **2** organic (plausibly independent: news, viral posts, fandoms, conversation) or **3**
can't tell; it saves and moves on. **n** adds a note, arrows move. You never see the detector's
status, score, signals, member roles or analyst/source checks, and you shouldn't look the group up on the dashboard.
Two people label every item separately; when both are done, the *disagreements* view shows both

## 2. Product

Name: **Shill or Chill** (decided 2026-11-13 22:42 by Justinas; replaces the working name "Noise Radar"). Tagline: "Shill or chill? We check the receipts." Tone: youthful and internet-native (stock-forum, meme-page, reels culture), but never at the cost of the honesty story.
- User-facing verdict labels map 1:1 to `clusters.status` (the DB/API values don't change): `coordinated` → 🚩 **Shill** · `likely_organic` → 😎 **Chill** · `insufficient` → 🤷 **Can't tell (yet)**.
- Wording guard: "shill" appears only in the product name, headings and the verdict label for a cluster. Evidence text describes behaviour ("31 accounts, same link, 94 s") and never calls a specific account or person "a shill": we can prove coordination, not payment or intent. The methodology page says this.
- Supporting copy (optional): "Receipts" for the evidence panel, "Certified organic" for a Chill verdict.
- Infra names stay as they are (repo `gemini-4-braincells`, `/opt/noise-radar`, `~/.config/noise-radar`, the `noise-radar.` subdomain); only user-facing text changes.

A live monitor that detects coordinated amplification (bot or campaign behaviour) on Bluesky, explains each flagged cluster with evidence, and reports its own measured error rates.

Thesis, and what we must not build: the generic "paste a post and an LLM says propaganda" tool. Most teams will build that. We detect **coordination between accounts** from behaviour signals, then use LLMs only to explain and to read media. Hostinger judges "strength and honesty of detection logic, including how you handle false positives" over UI. Every design choice should favour measurable precision, calibrated confidence and explicit abstention.

Hard requirement: deployed and running live on **Hostinger** infrastructure with a **public URL** by the end of the hackathon. If it isn't live on Hostinger, we're disqualified from the main prize.

def organic_guards(
    members: list[str],
    sk: list[Key],
    info: dict[str, AccountInfo],
    wd: WindowData,
    cfg: DetectorConfig,
) -> list[Signal]:
    out = []
    known = [info[d] for d in members if d in info]
    aged = [a for a in known if a.age_days is not None and a.followers is not None]
    if len(aged) >= cfg.min_cluster_size:
        est = sorted(a.did for a in aged if a.age_days > 365 and (a.followers or 0) >= 100)
        share = len(est) / len(aged)
        ages = np.array([a.age_days for a in aged])
        out.append(
            Signal(
                "guard",
                "established_accounts",
                _r(share),
                f"{len(est)} of {len(aged)} accounts are over a year old with 100+ followers "
                f"(account ages span {ages.min():.0f}-{ages.max():.0f} days)",
                {
                    "established": len(est),
                    "with_age": len(aged),
                    "age_min_days": _r(ages.min()),
                    "age_max_days": _r(ages.max()),
                },
                dids=est,
                polarity="against",
            )
        )
    if sk:
        excl = [len(k.accounts) / max(k.total_accounts, 1) for k in sk]  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        mean_excl = float(np.mean(excl))
        out.append(
            Signal(
                "guard",
                "part_of_wider_crowd",
                _r(1 - mean_excl),
                f"on average only {mean_excl:.0%} of the accounts sharing these items "
                "in the window are in this cluster (a wider crowd is doing the same thing)",
                {"mean_exclusivity": _r(mean_excl), "shared_keys": len(sk)},
                polarity="against",
            )
        )
    handles = [
        (a.did, a.handle.lower(), a.age_days)
        for a in known
        if a.handle and a.handle != "handle.invalid"
    ]
    if len(handles) >= cfg.min_cluster_size:
        domains: dict[str, list] = {}
        for d, h, age in handles:
            parts = h.split(".")
            if len(parts) >= 3:  # sub.domain.tld: the operator's own domain
                domains.setdefault(".".join(parts[-2:]), []).append((d, age))
        common = {dom: v for dom, v in domains.items() if dom not in _SHARED_HANDLE_DOMAINS}
        if common:
            dom = max(sorted(common), key=lambda k: len(common[k]))
            group = common[dom]
            old = [d for d, age in group if age is not None and age >= 180]
            share = len(group) / len(handles)
            out.append(
                Signal(
                    "guard",
                    "transparent_automation",
                    _r(share * (len(old) / len(group)) if len(group) >= 2 else 0),
                    f"{len(group)} of {len(handles)} accounts openly share the handle domain {dom} "
                    f"({len(old)} over 6 months old): one declared operator, e.g. an automated "
                    "feed, rather than a covert campaign",
                    {"domain": dom, "accounts": len(group), "older_than_180d": len(old)},
                    dids=sorted(d for d, _ in group),
                    polarity="against",
                )
            )
    # Scheduled posting: independent bots that post "at the top of the hour" look synchronized.
    times = [u.t for k in sk if k.family == "content" for u in k.uses]
    if len(times) >= cfg.min_cluster_size:
        aligned = sum(1 for t in times if (t % 1800) < 90 or (t % 1800) > 1800 - 15)
        share = aligned / len(times)
        if share >= 0.5:
            out.append(
                Signal(
                    "guard",
                    "clock_aligned_posting",
                    _r(0.7 * share),
                    f"{aligned} of {len(times)} shared posts went out within 90 s after "
                    "a full or half hour (5% expected by chance): "
                    "scheduled bots can look synchronized without being coordinated",
                    {"aligned": aligned, "posts": len(times), "expected_share": 0.05},
                    polarity="against",
                )
            )
    # Declared automation: most accounts say in their bio or name that they are a bot, a feed or
    # automated alerts, and they aren't new. Openly automated services (traffic, weather, news
    # feeds) post in sync by design; that is not a covert campaign.
    aged_text = [a for a in known if a.age_days is not None and (a.description or a.display_name)]
    if len(aged_text) >= cfg.min_cluster_size:
        declared = sorted(
            a.did
            for a in aged_text
            if a.age_days >= 90
            and _DECLARED_BOT.search(f"{a.display_name or ''} {a.description or ''}")
        )
        if len(declared) >= 2:
            out.append(
                Signal(
                    "guard",
                    "declared_automation",
                    _r(len(declared) / len(aged_text)),
                    f"{len(declared)} of {len(aged_text)} accounts say in their name or bio that "
                    "they are a bot, a feed or automated alerts, and are over 90 days old: an "
                    "openly automated service posts in sync by design",
                    {"declared": len(declared), "with_bio_or_name": len(aged_text)},
                    dids=declared,
                    polarity="against",
                )
            )
    # Members talking to each other: replies from one member to another member's post. Rings
    # that broadcast (spam, like farms, reply floods into strangers' threads) almost never do;
    # friend groups, fandoms and role-play communities do it all the time.
    mset_c = set(members)
    ix_c = wd.index()
    to_members = [
        (p.did, p.reply_to)
        for d in sorted(mset_c)
        for p in ix_c.posts_by_did.get(d, ())
        if p.reply_to and _uri_did(p.reply_to) in mset_c and _uri_did(p.reply_to) != p.did
    ]
    if to_members:
        replying = {a for a, _ in to_members}
        m = len(members)
        score = min(1.0, len(replying) / m) * min(1.0, len(to_members) / (2 * m))
        out.append(
            Signal(
                "guard",
                "members_converse",
                _r(score),
                f"{len(replying)} of {m} accounts reply to each other ({len(to_members)} replies "
                "between members): a conversation among people who know each other, not a "
                "broadcast",
                {"members_replying": len(replying), "replies_between_members": len(to_members)},
                uris=sorted({u for _, u in to_members})[:50],
                dids=sorted(replying),
                polarity="against",
            )
        )
    langs: dict[str, int] = {}
    mset = set(members)
    ix = wd.index()
    for p in (p for d in mset for p in ix.posts_by_did.get(d, ())):
        if p.langs:
            langs[p.langs[0]] = langs.get(p.langs[0], 0) + 1
    if sum(langs.values()) >= cfg.min_cluster_size and len(langs) >= 3:
        total = sum(langs.values())
        ent = -sum((c / total) * math.log(c / total) for c in langs.values()) / math.log(len(langs))
        out.append(
            Signal(
                "guard",
                "language_diversity",
                _r(ent * min(1.0, len(langs) / 4)),
                f"members post in {len(langs)} languages",
                {"languages": dict(sorted(langs.items()))},
                polarity="against",
            )
        )
    return out

"""POST /api/analyze: a judge's own input.

Answers two separate questions and never mixes them up:
1. Is this account, link or text part of a cluster we monitor? Then that cluster's detector
   status and analyst verdict apply.
2. Otherwise: live web findings (Oxylabs) about the link or text. These describe where content
   appears; they are weaker evidence and are never turned into a coordination verdict.
"""

from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends

from api.deps import get_checker, get_store
from api.schemas import AnalyzeRequest, AnalyzeResponse, ClusterSummary, WebFinding
from api.store import Store
from signals.textnorm import normalize_url
from sources.checker import SourceChecker
from sources.links import claim_phrase
from sources.models import ClusterPost

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/analyze", tags=["analyze"])

NOT_IN_WINDOW = (
    "Not seen in the clusters we monitor, so there is no coordination verdict. "
    "Coordination is a property of many accounts acting together; one post or link alone "
    "cannot show it. The web findings below only describe where the content appears."
)


@router.post("", response_model=AnalyzeResponse)
def analyze(
    req: AnalyzeRequest,
    store: Annotated[Store, Depends(get_store)],
    checker: Annotated[SourceChecker | None, Depends(get_checker)],
) -> AnalyzeResponse:
    clusters: dict[int, ClusterSummary] = {}
    notes: list[str] = []
    handle = (req.handle or "").strip().removeprefix("@")
    url = (req.url or "").strip()
    text = (req.text or "").strip()

    if handle:
        clusters.update((c.id, c) for c in store.clusters_for_handle(handle))
    if url:
        variants = sorted({u for u in (url, normalize_url(url)) if u})  # stored normalized
        clusters.update((c.id, c) for c in store.clusters_for_url(variants))
    phrase = claim_phrase([text]) if text else None
    if phrase:  # short text would match unrelated posts, so it is not looked up
        clusters.update((c.id, c) for c in store.clusters_for_text(phrase))

    findings: list[WebFinding] = []
    if (url or phrase) and checker is None:
        notes.append("Live web checks are not configured on this server.")
    elif url or phrase:
        # One synthetic post lets the cluster checker run unchanged on ad-hoc input.
        post = ClusterPost(did="adhoc", text=text or None, embed_urls=[url] if url else [])
        findings = [WebFinding(**e.model_dump()) for e in checker.check([post])]
        if not findings:
            notes.append("The live web check returned nothing usable for this input.")
    elif text:
        notes.append("Text too short for a reliable exact-phrase web search (needs 5+ words).")

    if clusters:
        return AnalyzeResponse(
            status="matched",
            clusters=sorted(clusters.values(), key=lambda c: c.window_end, reverse=True),
            web_findings=findings,
            notes=notes,

"""Source checks for one cluster: what its shared links say, and where its message appears.

Produces `SourceEvidence` items; storing them is `sources.store`'s job. Every item carries the
URL it came from. Failures are logged and skipped: a missing check is not evidence either way.
"""

import logging
import time
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from typing import Protocol

from sources.links import claim_phrase, domain, top_links
from sources.models import ClusterPost, PageFacts, SearchHit, SourceEvidence
from sources.oxylabs import OxylabsError

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SCRAPE_MODEL = "oxylabs-web-api/scrape"
SEARCH_MODEL = "oxylabs-web-api/search"
EARLIEST_NOTE = "Earliest date shown among the top search results. A hint, not proof of origin."


class WebClient(Protocol):
    def search(self, query: str, max_results: int = 10) -> list[SearchHit]: ...
    def scrape_facts(self, url: str) -> PageFacts: ...


class SourceChecker:
    def __init__(
        self,
        client: WebClient,
        *,
        max_links: int = 3,
        max_hits: int = 8,
        cache_ttl_s: float = 6 * 3600,
        failure_ttl_s: float = 1800,
    ):
        self._client = client
        self._max_links = max_links
        self._max_hits = max_hits
        self._ttl = cache_ttl_s
        self._failure_ttl = failure_ttl_s
        # key -> (expires_at, value); value None = the call failed recently, don't retry yet
        self._cache: dict[str, tuple[float, object]] = {}

    def check(
        self, posts: Sequence[ClusterPost], *, stored: Mapping[str, dict] | None = None
    ) -> list[SourceEvidence]:
        """Evidence for checks not already stored. `stored` maps evidence key -> detail."""
        stored = stored or {}
        n_accounts = len({p.did for p in posts})
        out: list[SourceEvidence] = []

        for url, shared_by in top_links(posts, self._max_links):
            key = f"page:{url}"
            if key in stored:  # scraped in an earlier pass: reuse its headline, don't re-scrape
                headline = stored[key].get("headline")
            else:
                facts = self._cached(f"scrape:{url}", lambda u=url: self._client.scrape_facts(u))
                if facts is None:
                    continue
                out.append(_page_evidence(key, facts, shared_by, n_accounts))
                headline = facts.headline
            if headline:
                ev = self._search_evidence("headline", headline, stored)
                if ev:
                    out.append(ev)

        phrase = claim_phrase(p.text for p in posts)
        if phrase:
            ev = self._search_evidence("post_text", phrase, stored)
            if ev:
                out.append(ev)
        return out

    def _search_evidence(
        self, purpose: str, phrase: str, stored: Mapping[str, dict]
    ) -> SourceEvidence | None:
        key = f"search:{purpose}:{phrase.lower()}"
        if key in stored:
            return None
        query = f'"{phrase}"'
        hits = self._cached(f"search:{query}", lambda: self._client.search(query, self._max_hits))
        if hits is None:
            return None
        return _search_evidence(key, purpose, phrase, query, hits)

    def _cached(self, key: str, fetch):
        now = time.monotonic()
        hit = self._cache.get(key)
        if hit and now < hit[0]:
            return hit[1]
        try:
            value = fetch()
        except OxylabsError as exc:
            log.warning("source check skipped for %.0fs (%s): %s", self._failure_ttl, key, exc)
            self._cache[key] = (now + self._failure_ttl, None)
            return None
        self._cache[key] = (now + self._ttl, value)
        return value


def _page_evidence(key: str, f: PageFacts, shared_by: int, n_accounts: int) -> SourceEvidence:
    title = f'"{f.headline}"' if f.headline else domain(f.final_url)
    by = ", ".join(x for x in (f.publisher, f.author, f.published_at) if x) or "publisher unknown"
    summary = f"Linked page shared by {shared_by} of {n_accounts} accounts: {title} ({by})."
    if f.http_status and f.http_status != 200:
        summary += f" The page returned HTTP {f.http_status}."
    return SourceEvidence(
        summary=summary,
        detail={
            "key": key,
            "type": "linked_page",
            "url": f.url,
            "final_url": f.final_url,
            "domain": domain(f.final_url),
            "http_status": f.http_status,
            "shared_by_accounts": shared_by,
            "cluster_accounts": n_accounts,
            "publisher": f.publisher,
            "author": f.author,
            "published_at": f.published_at,
            "headline": f.headline,
            "claims": f.claims,
        },
        source_url=f.final_url,
        model=SCRAPE_MODEL,

    key: str, purpose: str, phrase: str, query: str, hits: list[SearchHit]

    dated = [h for h in hits if h.published_hint]

        summary=summary,
        detail={
            "key": key,
            "type": "web_search",
            "purpose": purpose,
            "query": query,
            "distinct_domains": len(domains),
            "hits": [

                    "position": h.position,
                    "published_hint": h.published_hint.isoformat() if h.published_hint else None,

            "earliest_dated": (

            ),
            "note": EARLIEST_NOTE,
        },

"""Pure helpers: which links a cluster shares, and which phrase to search the web for."""

import re
from collections import Counter
from collections.abc import Iterable
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from signals.textnorm import normalize_url
from sources.models import ClusterPost

# Links that point back into Bluesky itself say nothing about outside sources.
SKIP_HOSTS = frozenset({"bsky.app", "go.bsky.app"})
MEDIA_SUFFIXES = (".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".gif", ".webp", ".mp4", ".mov", ".m3u8")

_URL = re.compile(r"https?://\S+")
_MENTION_OR_TAG = re.compile(r"(?<!\w)[@#][\w.\-]+")
_SENTENCE_SPLIT = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n+")


def checkable_url(url: str) -> str | None:
    """The canonical URL (same form ingest stores) if it is worth a source check, else None."""
    norm = normalize_url(url)
    if not norm:
        return None
    parts = urlsplit(norm)
    host = parts.hostname or ""
    if host in SKIP_HOSTS or host == "localhost" or re.fullmatch(r"[\d.:]+", host):
        return None
    if parts.path.lower().endswith(MEDIA_SUFFIXES):
        return None
    return norm


def domain(url: str) -> str:
    return (urlsplit(url).hostname or "").lower().removeprefix("www.")


def top_links(posts: Iterable[ClusterPost], k: int) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
    """The k links shared by the most distinct accounts: [(normalized_url, n_accounts)]."""
    sharers: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    for p in posts:
        for raw in p.embed_urls:
            url = checkable_url(raw)
            if url:
                sharers.setdefault(url, set()).add(p.did)
    ranked = sorted(sharers.items(), key=lambda kv: (-len(kv[1]), kv[0]))
    return [(url, len(dids)) for url, dids in ranked[:k]]


def _clean(text: str) -> str:
    text = _MENTION_OR_TAG.sub(" ", _URL.sub(" ", text))
    return re.sub(r"[ \t]+", " ", text).strip()


def claim_phrase(
    texts: Iterable[str | None], *, min_words: int = 5, max_words: int = 12
) -> str | None:
    """A distinctive phrase from the cluster's most repeated text, for an exact-phrase search.

    Takes the longest sentence of the most common (cleaned) text and cuts it to `max_words`.
    None when no sentence has at least `min_words` words: short phrases match too much of the web.
    """
    cleaned = [c for c in (_clean(t) for t in texts if t) if c]
    if not cleaned:
        return None
    common, _ = Counter(c.lower() for c in cleaned).most_common(1)[0]
    original = next(c for c in cleaned if c.lower() == common)
    sentences = [s.strip(" \"'“”") for s in _SENTENCE_SPLIT.split(original)]
    best = max(sentences, key=lambda s: len(s.split()), default="")
    words = best.split()
    if len(words) < min_words:
        return None
    return " ".join(words[:max_words]).rstrip(",;:")

def normalize_text(text: str | None) -> str:
    """Lowercase, NFKC, strip URLs, @mentions, emoji and punctuation; keep words and #tags."""
    if not text:
        return ""
    t = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text).lower()
    t = _URL_RE.sub(" ", t)
    t = _BARE_DOMAIN_RE.sub(" ", t)
    t = _MENTION_RE.sub(" ", t)
    t = _NON_WORD_RE.sub(" ", t)  # emoji, punctuation, symbols
    t = t.replace("_", " ")
    return _WS_RE.sub(" ", t).strip()


def tokens(norm_text: str) -> list[str]:
    return norm_text.split() if norm_text else []


def text_hash(text: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Stable 16-hex hash of the normalised text, or None when nothing is left after normalising."""
    norm = normalize_text(text)
    if not norm:
        return None
    return hashlib.blake2b(norm.encode(), digest_size=8).hexdigest()


MAX_URL_LEN = 1000  # Postgres index entries max out near 2.7 kB; real links are far shorter


def normalize_url(url: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Canonical form for comparing links: https, lowercase host without www., no fragment,
    no tracking params, sorted query, no trailing slash. Resolves nothing (no network)."""
    if not url:
        return None
    url = url.strip()
    if not url:
        return None
    if "://" not in url:
        if _SCHEME_RE.match(url):  # mailto:, javascript:, data: ...
            return None
        url = "https://" + url
    try:
        parts = urlsplit(url)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if parts.scheme.lower() not in ("http", "https"):
        return None
    host = (parts.hostname or "").lower().rstrip(".")
    if not host:
        return None
    if host.startswith("www."):
        host = host[4:]
    try:
        port = parts.port
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if port and port not in (80, 443):
        host = f"{host}:{port}"
    query = [
        (k, v)
        for k, v in parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True)
        if not k.lower().startswith("utm_") and k.lower() not in _TRACKING_PARAMS
    ]
    query.sort()
    path = parts.path or ""
    if path.endswith("/"):
        path = path.rstrip("/")
    out = urlunsplit(("https", host, path, urlencode(query), ""))
    return out[:MAX_URL_LEN]


def url_domain(normalized_url: str) -> str:
    """Host part of a normalised URL (e.g. 'example.com')."""
    return urlsplit(normalized_url).hostname or ""
